thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PAGER: gpu-queue-growth (p0) — queue length crossing alert threshold for model: gpt-neox-8k-serving. Impact: sustained enqueue rate > provisioned throughput. paging oncall maya.

maya: seeing huge queue growth on the inference queue, latency for requests is spiking to 6-12s p95. Paging now. Starting timeline notes.

liam: can you confirm autoscaler status? last deploy to autoscaler was ~0400 UTC yesterday.

rachel: from dashboards — autoscaler reports max_replicas hit (pool: gpu-pool-east), scale events suppressed due to scale_cap=32. queue length ~18k requests across shards.

tom: ml_serving: we rolled continuous-batching v2 config in the last rollout (team: eng-runtime) at 0330; it tightened batch window and changed prefix cache TTL to 60s for memory reduction. Suspect perf regression.

maya: confirmed. prefix cache miss rate jumped from ~4% to ~38% after that rollout. throughput per GPU dropped by ~22%.

ops_lead: immediate mitigation options: 1) revert continuous-batching params to previous stable, 2) manually increase autoscaler cap, 3) route high-volume customers to dedicated pool, 4) warm prefix cache. We should coordinate.

liam: I'm already on infra console. Manual scale bump possible but we need surge quota approval. How many extra nodes to meaningfully reduce queue?

rachel: rough calc: at current throughput, adding 8 GPUs reduces queue by ~30% over 15m. But if batching config stays degraded, we keep losing headroom.

maya: customers reporting elevated latency. product_support — any active customer tickets?

product_support: open cases: 3 enterprise customers (one frontline web app), all posting timeouts and 5xxs. We'll post status update if we have a mitigation ETA.

ml_serving: pushing to revert continuous-batching config now. Reverting prefix cache TTL to 300s and batch window to previous values. Deploy command:
```
cictl deploy --service=continuous-batching --env=prod --image=cbatch:v2026.02.12-rev
```

infra_sre: starting manual autoscaler override to +10 replicas on gpu-pool-east:
```
infractl pools update gpu-pool-east --max-replicas=42 --force-override --reason="incident 1765432109 manual bump"
```

liam: applied override, new max=42. Scaling events are queued; starting node provisioning. ETA ~6-8m for GPUs to come up.

tom: revert deploy succeeded, rolling config now. Observability: prefix cache miss rate dropping in the canary region.

maya: real-time metrics: queue length dropping from 18k -> 11k after autoscaler bump and config revert, p95 latency down to ~2.3s. Still above normal but improving.

product_support: sending interim update to impacted customers: "We are actively mitigating a capacity and configuration issue impacting request latency. We expect significant improvement within 15 minutes"

rachel: note: there was also a scale-safety gating rule introduced last month that delays aggressive scaling when many shards report high eviction. Might be contributing to slower autoscale response. Need to audit postmortem.

ops_lead: for now mitigation = revert + manual bump + cache warmup. Assigning handoff to liam for infra follow-up and tom for serving follow-up. Maya handing oncall to liam at +00:30.

liam: taking over oncall. I'll watch provisioning and coordinate with SRE. I'll also request temporary surge quota from cloud for +12 GPUs if required.

ml_serving: additional step: toggled "aggressive_prefix_warmup" for hot models to true to populate caches faster. Command:
```
servingctl config set gpt-neox-8k-prefetch aggressive_prefix_warmup=true
```

maya: thanks. adding quick checklist for incident record:
- root cause hypothesis: continuous-batching config change reduced effective throughput + prefix cache TTL lowered causing high miss rate => autoscaler hit max => queue growth and throttling
- mitigations taken: revert config, manual autoscaler bump, prefix warmup, customer notifications
- impact: 3 enterprise customers saw degraded p95 latency (6-12s) and intermittent 5xx; internal SLO breach for 22 minutes
- owners: infra (liam), serving (tom), product_support (rachel)

product_support: posted status update. customers responded with controlled escalations; one requested dedicated capacity temporarily.

liam: cloud granted temporary surge quota +12 GPUs, provisioning in progress. Will monitor CPU/GPU churn.

rachel: dashboards show prefix cache miss rate back down to ~6% and per-GPU throughput within 95% of baseline. Queue down to 3k and counting.

ops_lead: OK let's stop paging. If metrics stay stable for 30m, we'll close pager. Keep the thread active for timeline & RCA notes.

maya: handing backnotes: please collect exact deploy hashes, autoscaler events, and a list of customer request IDs impacted. We'll run a blameless postmortem tomorrow.

liam: noted. collecting logs:
```
# autoscaler events
infractl events list --pool=gpu-pool-east --since=1765432000
```

tom: I'll capture serving traces and the batching config diff:
```
git show origin/main:configs/continuous-batching.yaml@{2026-02-11}..origin/main:configs/continuous-batching.yaml@{2026-02-12}
```

product_support: I'll compile customer impact notes and prepare the email template for follow-up.

ops_lead: summary: incident mitigated via config rollback, manual scaling, and cache warmup. Action items: (1) revert gating on scale-safety rule for hot models or tune thresholds (owner: infra), (2) add canary test for prefix cache TTL changes (owner: ml_serving), (3) run load replay to validate throughput before deploys (owner: eng-runtime), (4) update runbook for autoscaler manual override (owner: ops).

maya: closing pager for now. oncall handover complete. We'll reconvene for a 30m post-incident sync and schedule RCA.
summary: GPU queue growth due to batching/prefix-cache config regression; autoscaler hit max cap. Mitigations: revert config, manual autoscaler bump, prefix warmup. Customer impact: elevated latency and 5xxs for 3 customers. Owners assigned for RCA.
